effort: Transfer force into a strong backward draw while maintaining grip and shoulder control.

explosive.name: Landmine Power Row — continuous hip-to-arm drive
explosive.job: Primary transfer of a small body impulse through the trunk into a forceful backward arm draw.
explosive.cue: Light two-hand sleeve grip; start in a short hinge. Extend hips slightly as elbows draw toward lower ribs in one connected pull, then lower/reset under control. No separate deadlift rep, shrug, jump, rotation or bar release.
explosive.replacement: the paused arm-driven landmine row if hip-to-arm timing is not controlled, or a light two-hand kettlebell row if bar fit fails
explosive.identity: Proposed continuous power-row execution; related to landmine row/hinge-to-row library but no exact profile ID asserted
explosive.uniqueness_reason: First deliberate hip-to-arm force transfer in a pull, inspired by OTA's ballistic sled-row concept but using available equipment. It changes the force-production task; the earlier strict rows explicitly prohibited hip drive.
explosive.key: Landmine Power Row — continuous hip-to-arm drive

explosive.name: Band Row — alternating arm draws from a fixed trunk
explosive.job: Transfer backward pulling effort between arms without rocking the torso.
explosive.cue: Permitted seated foot anchoring; alternate four draws per arm while the other hand remains forward. Each draw returns under control before the next arm begins. Eight total draws, not eight per arm.
explosive.replacement: four bilateral seated band-row cycles if alternating control is unsuitable; record the changed laterality and task-rep count
explosive.identity: band-row parent; alternating draw execution proposed
explosive.uniqueness_reason: The alternating arm-force sequence differs from prior simultaneous band rows and from hand-over-hand rope translation. It is a related row task, not a new family or an implement-only substitution.
explosive.key: Band Row — alternating arm draws from a fixed trunk

explosive.name: Band Biceps Curl — loaded return into quick reversal
explosive.job: Carry force through the elbow after a controlled lengthening rather than a swinging shoulder start.
explosive.cue: Band securely beneath both feet, elbows at ribs; lower for 2 s to comfortable near-extension then reverse promptly into flexion. Avoid snapping full elbow extension or leaning.
explosive.replacement: a paused rapid neutral-grip curl if reversal control is absent
explosive.identity: Proposed exact execution; no verified canonical identifier
explosive.uniqueness_reason: Related to Class 3 rapid elbow flexion; the controlled reversal is explicit. A heavier hammer curl was rejected because load escalation does not create a new drill and would add fatigue.
explosive.key: Band Biceps Curl — loaded return into quick reversal

explosive.name: Medicine Ball Overhead Slam — single arm, no trunk rotation
explosive.job: Express each shoulder's downward force independently while remaining square.
explosive.cue: Use a small light low-rebound ball that one hand controls; raise to comfortable overhead reach, pull down to a floor target in front of that side. Feet planted, no crunch or twist, no catching the rebound.
explosive.replacement: four two-hand arm-driven slams total if one-arm ball fit or overhead control is unsuitable; if the floor is unsuitable use a single-arm rapid band pulldown and log zero releases
explosive.identity: medicine-ball-overhead-slam parent; unilateral arm-driven variant proposed
explosive.uniqueness_reason: Related to Class 3 bilateral slams but now requires independent arm control without counter-rotation. Only two throws per arm; a rotational slam would leave the requested straight-line force focus.
explosive.key: Medicine Ball Overhead Slam — single arm, no trunk rotation

explosive.name: Kneeling Medicine Ball Chest Pass — tall kneeling, no hip swing
explosive.job: Preserve a small clean forward release while pulling is the main demand.
explosive.cue: Tall knees, still chest start; push forward with both arms and stay upright.
explosive.replacement: a seated chest pass if kneeling is uncomfortable, or a self-anchored band chest press if release clearance fails
explosive.uniqueness_reason: Explicit Class 2 repeat, reduced to one set. A moving chest pass was considered but would add step coordination beside the new body-assisted row; removing leg drive keeps the support job focused.
explosive.key: Kneeling Medicine Ball Chest Pass — tall kneeling, no hip swing

explosive.name: Band Straight-Arm Pulldown — rapid shoulder extension
explosive.job: Finish with a short shoulder-driven pull that does not add elbow-flexor fatigue.
explosive.cue: Rated overhead attachment; softly fixed elbows, fast pull from comfortable reach toward thighs, return 2 s with ribs quiet.
explosive.replacement: a light controlled rapid dumbbell pullover toward vertical if no suitable attachment exists; record the changed force curve
explosive.uniqueness_reason: Class 2 repeat at three reps. A new grip-dominant drill was rejected after rope/alternating pulls and curls; shoulder-only force is the needed complementary job.
explosive.key: Band Straight-Arm Pulldown — rapid shoulder extension

resilience.name: Band Face Pull — light controlled draw
resilience.job: Lightly strengthen control of the shoulder-blade and upper-arm position during the high-force draw.
resilience.cue: Band on an inspected chest/face-height attachment; draw toward brow with elbows comfortably out, hold 1 s, return 2 s without leaning.
resilience.replacement: a light unanchored band pull-apart if the attachment is unavailable
resilience.key: Band Face Pull — light controlled draw

resilience.name: Dumbbell Wrist Flexion — forearm supported
resilience.job: Lightly load wrist/forearm control that maintains grip alignment during pulling.
resilience.cue: Palm up, forearm supported on thigh; small comfortable wrist motion, lift 1 s and lower 3 s, no finger rolling or forced stretch.
resilience.replacement: unloaded wrist flexion through the same comfortable range if the lightest dumbbell is excessive
resilience.identity: Proposed exact execution; no verified canonical identifier

primary.name: One-Arm Row — dumbbell, hand and knee on bench
primary.job: Priority horizontal pulling strength: move the load through the shoulder and elbow while keeping the body still.
primary.cue: Draw elbow toward hip, hold 1 s, lower 2 s; stop before the shoulder rolls forward or the trunk turns.
primary.replacement: a thigh-supported dumbbell row with the same arm path if a bench does not fit

primary.name: Band Lat Pulldown — kneeling, two arms
primary.job: Load the downward arm draw needed for assisted pull-up force without another horizontal row set.
primary.cue: Use a manufacturer-permitted band on an inspected overhead anchor; kneel tall, draw elbows to ribs, hold 1 s, return 2 s; no lumbar lean.
primary.replacement: a foot-supported pull-up with comfortable grip and enough assistance to preserve 2–3 RIR; otherwise a supported row with the vertical-pull gap recorded
primary.identity: band-lat-pulldown; resistance-band-body-resistance-all-cards.json; exact setup must be inspected

primary.name: Dumbbell Rear-Delt Row — bilateral, hinged
primary.job: Strengthen the wider-elbow backward draw that controls the arm-open position.
primary.cue: Hold a still hinge; elbows about 60 degrees from torso, pull to upper ribs, hold 1 s, lower 2 s.
primary.replacement: a chest-supported version only on an inspected bench with adequate arm clearance

primary.name: Dumbbell Hammer Curl — simultaneous arms
primary.job: Load elbow flexors for finishing the backward draw without another shoulder-extension set.
primary.cue: Upper arms stay at ribs; lift 1 s, hold 1 s, lower 2 s, without hip swing or wrist collapse.
primary.replacement: a lighter neutral-grip curl without body movement

primary.name: Floor Press — two dumbbells, neutral grip
primary.job: Main horizontal pressing force with a reproducible floor-limited range.
primary.cue: Lower 2 s, touch upper arms gently, pause 1 s, then press decisively; feet stay down. Coach supervises pickup/set-down.
primary.replacement: a lighter floor press through controlled comfortable range

primary.name: Dumbbell Skull Crusher — floor-supported
primary.job: Load elbow extension for the finish of a forceful press.
primary.cue: Neutral grips, upper arms near vertical; lower 2 s beside the ears, extend under control without shoulder swing.
primary.replacement: a lighter floor-supported elbow extension through comfortable range

progression: Class 7 prescribed 64 task reps across eleven unilateral-heavy primary bouts. This class returns to the already written Class 3 pulling allocation: One-Arm Row 2 × 6 per arm, Lat Pulldown 2 × 6, and one set each of rear-delt row, curl, Floor Press and elbow extension. That is eight rounds, ten bouts and 66 task reps. This returns to a known prescription, not an observed successful dose. The body-assisted speed row uses a light load independent of primary-row loading. Hold or regress if first-set mechanics or actual recovery does not support it; later progression requires reported control, reserve and recovery.
audit_findings: Main power rows remain six controlled pulls; no weight release, separate hinge exercise or jumping. Seven total throws, no catches or hand landings. The forearm/elbow overlap from alternating rows and curls is limited to one short set each; shoulder-only pulling avoids another elbow-flexion drill. One new force-transfer task, three related variants and two justified repeats are disclosed. No invented low-bar/rack station or sled is required.
next_job: Class 9 should address a controlled step into forward projection, provided the actual athlete can maintain the release line and the entire step/ball path fits inspected space.
